correctness.rationale: Two distinct packaged verifier implementations were executed successfully: 3125 unique vertices; every one of 4881250 unordered vertex pairs tested by exact integer square equality (Python isqrt, C++ corrected integer128 sqrt); 14856 edges; all indexed i<j<k clique triples covered, yielding 288 triangles with primitive multiplicities 144+144. All 41328 unordered triangle pairs checked for intersections: 174 isolates and 57 nonadjacent pairs, split 9 single-vertex and 48 double-vertex intersections. A 231-element disjoint packing and 231-element triangle-hitting set were explicitly constructed and checked. The overlap matching is also proved algebraically from the distinct 2-adic coordinate valuations and the two possible multiplier ratios 21/5 and 275/63, giving 48 and 9 pairs. The deductions proving optimality then use the matching decomposition. This is a finite exact theorem, not an extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The original 2026 prime-power box paper proves asymptotic independence bounds; Knill’s 2022 Babylonian graph paper supplies the known triangle/brick equivalence and both known primitive brick examples; OEIS and a bounded public database list Euler bricks in different domains. The finite classification relies on independently reproduced exhaustive programs rather than a compact handwritten Diophantine classification.

value.rationale: The fifth box is the first where the recently studied Pythagorean-leg graph is nonbipartite, so the exact triangle hypergraph is a natural missing local invariant. This classifies every obstruction of length three, not just a chosen example; the unexpectedly sparse intersection pattern has an exact extremal interpretation as matching packing and transversal number 231, providing explicit finite structure relevant to the independence problem. The seeds themselves and elementary gcd scaling are not claimed original; the value is the complete box-filtered classification and optimal triangle hypergraph invariants. No assertion that this solves f(5) is made.
